newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom bill faces first Senate debate Wed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom bill faces first Senate debate Wed.

text.p: A bill regulating Brazil's telecommunications sector will be discussed simultaneously in three Senate committees Wednesday, the first step towards approval of the legislation in the upper house, officials said.

The economic affairs, infrastructure and constitution and justice committees would meet jointly at 1000 local/1300 GMT to begin debating the bill which paves the way for privatization of the Telebras system, the officials said.
An aide to Senator Hugo Napoleao, one of three senators appointed to oversee the legislation through committee-level proceedings, said she expected voting on the bill would only take place next week.
"There will almost certainly be a request for more time," she said.

Earlier Tuesday, Communications Minister Sergio Motta told local newswire Invest News he expected the bill would clear the committees and be ready for a final vote on the floor of the Senate by July 23.

Government whips will seek to maintain the bill as it was approved in the Chamber of Deputies earlier this month. If major changes were made to the bill in the Senate, it would then have to go back to the lower house, delaying its full approval.
The bill does limit foreign capital in Brazilian telecommunications operators but allows the president of the republic to set such restrictions on a case-by-case basis.
It also creates a new regulator for the sector and lays down rules for private operators.
